baseline.name: Our re-implementation of the Claw Guard design, adapted to NEAR Intents token_diff (not the deployed Claw Guard product)
adaptations: Venue: the owner's own Intents account holds the assets; the owner registers the guard's derived Ed25519 key there with add_public_key (Claw Guard: owner approves the derived address as a Hyperliquid API wallet). Unlike an API wallet, an Intents key is not trade-only; only the guard's payload construction restricts it.
Payload: NEP-413 token_diff over exactly USDC and wNEAR, signer = owner, built by the guard; Ed25519 domain 1 instead of secp256k1 domain 0.
Deadline: finite order TTL of 60 s, the mandate's value (Claw Guard's Hyperliquid orders carry no expiry).
Nonce: 32-byte legacy (non-versioned) nonce derived from the receipt id, accepted by verifier v0.4.5.
Caps in USDC units: per-order token and notional caps, daily notional cap, daily order count, permission expiry; notional of a wNEAR sell is the agent's minimum USDC (Claw Guard Q-42 analog).
Omitted as irrelevant to these cases: guardian role, set_rules loosening delay, receipt ring buffer, storage reserve rule, mainnet refusal, Hyperliquid/EVM encoders.

assertions.description: Permitted order signed by the guard and relayed: executed against the baseline and classified from chain state
Over-cap order (per-order notional cap + 1 unit): executed against the baseline and classified from chain state
Compromised agent key: withdrawal/transfer request, direct verifier and MPC calls: executed against the baseline and classified from chain state
Published signature with a failed signer callback, relayed independently: executed against the baseline and classified from chain state
Withheld signed order relayed after the guard's revocation (pause + remove_agent): executed against the baseline and classified from chain state
Withheld signed order relayed after the owner removes the derived key from the Intents account: executed against the baseline and classified from chain state
The same withheld order relayed after regrant: executed against the baseline and classified from chain state
Strand owner assets by disabling the agent and the signer: executed against the baseline and classified from chain state

cases.threat: Permitted order signed by the guard and relayed
cases.summary: Harness control: a permitted USDC->wNEAR order executes on the pinned verifier.
The guard evaluates the per-order cap before requesting a signature.

cases.threat: Compromised agent key: withdrawal/transfer request, direct verifier and MPC calls
cases.summary: Function-call key restricted to propose_order; the guard only builds token_diff payloads.

cases.threat: Published signature with a failed signer callback, relayed independently
cases.summary: Our re-implementation follows Claw Guard's design of releasing a reservation when on_signed sees a failure; a signature disclosed by the signer still executes, so executed notional is no longer counted.

cases.threat: Withheld signed order relayed after the guard's revocation (pause + remove_agent)
cases.summary: As documented in Claw Guard's Q-45 and re-implemented here: pause and remove_agent stop later proposals only; issued signatures stay valid.

cases.threat: Withheld signed order relayed after the owner removes the derived key from the Intents account
cases.summary: Venue-side key removal (the Intents analog of Claw Guard's documented Q-45 mitigation on Hyperliquid) makes the withheld order fail.

relay.error: Error { repr: Custom { kind: Execution, error: ActionError(ActionError { index: Some(0), kind: FunctionCallError(ExecutionError("Smart contract panicked: public key 'ed25519:AyKcV4q2cN9nsv7dxtHdicuFNZfXsXHAL4j15AuznyWB' doesn't exist for account 'owner.test.near'")) }) } }

cases.threat: The same withheld order relayed after regrant
cases.summary: Fixed derivation path: regrant restores the identical key, so withheld pre-revocation orders become executable again while unexpired.

cases.threat: Revocation during a pending key-registration callback
cases.summary: The guard has no key lifecycle: the owner registers and removes the derived key directly on the verifier, outside the guard. Not executed.
The guard has no key lifecycle: the owner registers and removes the derived key directly on the verifier, outside the guard. Not executed.

cases.threat: Aggregate outstanding exposure of signed-but-unsettled orders
cases.summary: The guard counts signed notional per UTC day only; it has no outstanding-exposure accounting or settlement-based release. Not executed.

cases.threat: Strand owner assets by disabling the agent and the signer
cases.summary: Assets stay in the owner's own Intents account; the owner's predecessor-authorized mt_transfer needs no agent, signer or oracle.
